title: Listening ear activated: the instant lock-in reaction
summary: Look bored, then lock in the second someone says the one thing you care about. AI writes the trigger lines for your niche.
why: Ramdam's TikTok trends roundup lists "Listening ear activated" in its October 19, 2026 update: creators look distracted, then go fully alert when a trigger line plays, with a text overlay that sets up the situation.
steps: Use the main prompt to get trigger lines: the one sentence that would make you stop everything and listen.
Film yourself bored or half-listening for 2 or 3 seconds (scrolling, staring out the window, slumped in a chair).
On the trigger, snap to full attention: sit up, lean in, turn your head slowly toward the camera.
Add the overlay text and line up the sound so the switch happens right on the trigger.

prompts.label: Main prompt
prompts.text: I'm filming a reaction clip where I'm bored, then I suddenly lock in when someone says something I care about. My niche is [your hobby, job or topic]. Write 10 overlay lines in this style: "When someone tells me [the thing that makes me pay attention]". Make each one specific to people in my niche, a little funny and under 25 words. No brand names, no real people.

prompts.label: Variation: everyday life
prompts.text: Write 8 "listening ear activated" overlay lines about ordinary life in Canada in fall and early winter, for example someone mentioning leftover Halloween candy, a snow day, a long weekend or free parking. Each line starts with "When someone says…". Short, playful and kind.

prompts.label: Variation: small business
prompts.text: I run a [type of business]. Write 6 "listening ear activated" overlay lines where I perk up when a customer or friend mentions something I love to help with. Start each with "When someone tells me…". Keep them honest, warm and under 25 words. Don't make claims I can't back up, and don't mention competitors.

prompts.label: Variation: shot list
prompts.text: Here's my overlay line: [paste it]. Write a shot list for a 6-second vertical phone video: what I'm doing while I'm bored, the exact moment I switch, and three ways to show I'm now fully listening. Keep it simple enough to film alone with my phone on a shelf.

tips: The switch is the whole joke. Make the bored part really bored and the lock-in really sharp.
Film on a shelf or tripod so you can do it in one take.
Pick a trigger your viewers will recognize right away. If they have to think, the moment is lost.
If a friend or family member appears in the clip, ask them first.
